findings.title: Debug logging left in at Error level, dumping every ID of every batch
findings.body: Six new `r.log.Error(...)` calls were added in `CleanAnnotations` (lines 534, 537, 554, 557) and `CleanOrphanedAnnotationTags` (lines 576, 579). These are informational/debug messages ("Annotations to clean by time", "cleaned tags", ...) emitted at ERROR level on every batch iteration of a job that runs continuously, and they include the full `ids` slice (up to `AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize` entries, 32767 in the new test) plus a nil `err`. Consequences: operators' error logs/alerting will fire on normal cleanup activity, and log volume/allocation becomes huge on large installations. These should be removed or downgraded to Debug without the full ID list.

findings.title: Cleanup job ticker reduced from 10 minutes to 1 minute
findings.body: `ticker := time.NewTicker(time.Minute * 1)` changes the global cleanup service interval from 10 minutes to 1 minute. This is unrelated to the annotation deadlock fix and looks like leftover local debugging. It makes every cleanup job (tmp file scan, expired snapshots, dashboard versions, images, annotations, invites, short URLs, query history row-limit enforcement) run 10x more often, multiplying DB and filesystem load on all Grafana instances; note also that `clean()` has a 9-minute timeout, so a long-running sweep is immediately followed by another. This change should be reverted unless intentional and documented.

findings.title: O(n^2) string building for SQLite inline ID list
findings.body: In `deleteByIDs`, the SQLite branch builds the ID list with `values = fmt.Sprintf("%s, %d", values, v)` inside a loop. Each iteration reallocates and copies the whole accumulated string, so for a batch of ~32k IDs (the size exercised by the new test) this performs ~32k allocations and copies of an ever-growing ~200KB string, i.e. gigabytes of memcpy per batch, repeated for every batch of the cleanup loop. Use a `strings.Builder` (or `strconv.AppendInt` into a byte slice, as done elsewhere in this file) instead.

findings.title: Placeholder-limit workaround only covers SQLite; large batch sizes can fail on MySQL/Postgres
findings.body: `deleteByIDs` only avoids bind parameters when `GetDBType() == migrator.SQLite && AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize > 999`. For MySQL and Postgres the code always emits one `?` per ID, but both have a hard limit of 65535 bind parameters per statement. An operator who sets `annotation_cleanup_job_batch_size` above 65535 will get a hard driver error on every cleanup cycle instead of a degraded-but-working job. Either cap the number of IDs per DELETE statement (chunking) regardless of dialect, or gate on `len(ids)` against a per-dialect limit.
